title: Traffic ecosystem failure-mode cookbook (stochastic safety lab)
body:
Purpose

This note collects failure modes we see (and simulate) across the traffic ecosystem during cross-functional rollouts, canaries, and A/B experiments. The goal is pragmatic: give operators a short-runbook and simulation recipes to reproduce noisy, stochastic failures and validate recovery/guardrails before live exposure.

Audience
- Release stewards, product owners running experiments
- SREs and infra engineers who own routing + autoscaling
- Solutions/SEs running customer canaries on Dedicated/Private

Quick summary / TL;DR
- Treat the routing stack + model variants + capacity tiers as one ecosystem — failures are often emergent, not single-point.
- Add small synthetic noise to traffic shapes in pre-prod to surface oscillation and cohort bleed.
- Monitor three classes of signals (latency/availability, semantic drift, economic): respond to the earliest reliable signal.
- Always have a fast, human-triggered escape hatch mapped to traffic slices.

Failure mode catalog (high-level)
1) Oscillation between tiers (cost-latency thrash)
   - What: traffic controller flips between cheap-quantized variant and full-precision variant due to marginal latency regressions; autoscaler then scales up/down causing more latency, cyclical.
   - Trigger examples: transient GPU GC, sudden token-length spike, model cache miss storm.
   - Detection: repeated latency spikes tied to specific route + model tag every ~2–10 minutes; CPU/GPU utilization trailing the latency curve.
   - Recovery checklist: pin the route to stable variant, pause autoscale for 5 minutes, route a small shadow slice to newer variant for further analysis.

2) Cohort contamination (A/B leakage)
   - What: user identifiers or cookie routing mislabels cohort -> metric contamination and invalid experiment.
   - Trigger examples: load balancer header rewrite, proxy cache returning wrong shard, mobile SDK caching cookie incorrectly.
   - Detection: sudden jump in user overlap between cohorts (dedup on user_id), unexpected conversion pattern in control.
   - Recovery checklist: immediately stop experiment, run membership audit (last 10k requests), restore prior routing rules and open an incident to trace proxy changes.

3) Semantic regression amplified by traffic slice (quality cliff)
   - What: new model variant has a low-probability hallucination that when exposed to a narrow cohort (e.g., legal docs) causes high false-positive rates.
   - Trigger examples: prompt templates in one product surface that are adversarial for the new model variant.
   - Detection: spike in semantic-safety alerts or manual-reviews for that slice; quality evals on production prompt set show >X% degradation.
   - Recovery checklist: rollback model variant for affected slice, create targeted prompt mitigations, add slice-specific guardrail tests to the rollout pipeline.

4) Economics shock (token-cost runaway)
   - What: generation policy change or prompt template alteration causes average response length to jump (-> cost spike).
   - Trigger examples: dynamic system message accidentally removed; sampling temparature increased; client-side prompt changed to append context repeatedly.
   - Detection: per-route cost-per-minute and per-token counters jump; budget burn alerts.
   - Recovery checklist: weight-limit throttle on the route, revert configuration, apply temporary hard cap on tokens-per-request.

5) Latency SLO iceberg (slow degradation)
   - What: 95p/99p latency creeps upward slowly, hitting SLO without obvious cause.
   - Trigger examples: KV cache eviction pattern changes, model kernel scheduler drifting due to core packing.
   - Detection: long tail percentiles trending upward for >48h; correlated increase across multiple models on same node pool.
   - Recovery checklist: progressive traffic drain from affected pool, trigger kernel fallback path, escalate to infra team for node-level investigation.

Signals and instrumentation (what to monitor first)
- Fast signals (seconds-minutes): p50/p95/p99 latency per-route, model-instance error rates, connection errors, queue length, token-rate.
- Cross-check signals (minutes): user-cohort overlap, backend cache miss ratio, model KV cache hit-rate.
- Quality signals (hours): eval set score regression, human-in-loop review volume, fallback-to-control ratio in experiments.
- Economic signals (minutes-hours): route token burn rate, cost per active user, burst bill estimator.

Operator playbooks (short)
- Immediate containment (first 10 min): 1) Activate the rollout pause button (freeze new exposure). 2) Shift 100% of the affected slice to control variant or fallback model. 3) Post to #release-ops with summary and initial mitigation action.
- Triage (10–60 min): 1) Pull the smallest reproducible traffic slice to reproduce in staging. 2) Run the pre-baked simulation case (see Simulations). 3) If contamination suspected, run membership audit and revoke experiment tokens.
- Resolution (60–240 min): 1) Decide rollback vs fix-forward. 2) If fix-forward, prepare a canary of the fix on a micro-slice with increased human review. 3) Capture learning: update the traffic-ecosystem test harness and checklist.

Simulation recipes (repro scripts / manual steps)
- Oscillation stress test (recommended before big rollout):
  1) In staging, run a 30-minute synthetic load with two client profiles: short prompt high QPS and long-prompt low QPS.
  2) Configure routing policy to prefer cheap variant but allow fallback after 200ms.
  3) Introduce random 50–350ms delay on model cache reads for 50% of requests to mimic cache churn.
  4) Observe controller behavior: are we toggling every 2–10 minutes? If yes, ttl smoothing or hysteresis required.

- Cohort bleed simulation:
  1) Create two test users and deliberately reassign the header that carries cohort id at the LB.
  2) Send mixed traffic and verify dedupe across cohorts.
  3) Validate experiment dashboard flags contamination and fails gate.

- Semantic cliff simulation (slice-specific):
  1) Assemble a production-like prompt set for the target slice (n=250).
  2) Run the new model variant offline and record hallucination/failure rate.
  3) Run the same set through routing with 10% live-exposure shadowing to human review.

Runbooks: templates (copy/modify in incidents)
- Slack short incident stub (post to #release-ops):
  - "INCIDENT: rollouts: route payments-checkout — latency spike detected on new-variant v1.2 (p95 1.6s -> 3.4s). Pausing exposure, shifting slice to control. Triage lead: @lina. Initial suspected cause: cache miss storm. More updates in thread."

- Pager escalation heuristic:
  - If p99 latency > 2x baseline for > 3 minutes AND token-cost increase > 30% -> page on-call SRE.
  - If cohort contamination confirmed -> page product owner + legal (if external customers affected).

Guardrails and automation recommendations
- Default micro-slices: every experiment must start with at least 3 orthogonal micro-slices (by country, product persona, and prompt-length) to reduce blind spots.
- Hysteresis on routing decisions: require 3 consecutive checks across 5 minutes before switching model variants.
- Circuit-breaker layers: per-slice token caps, per-route cost burn throttle, and immediate fallback route.
- Canary test harness: repository of scenario scripts that can be replayed against a fresh staging cluster in <10 minutes.

Postmortem checklist (for rollouts)
- Timestamped decision log exported from the Console for the rollout window.
- Membership audit spreadsheet for cohorts (include last touchpoint).
- Small corpus of failing prompts and human annotations.
- A recommended fix category: rollback / prompt-mitigation / routing-adjust / infra-hotfix.

Open questions / next experiments
- Can we synthesize a realistic cost-smoke test that runs for 24h without incurring major bills? (budget-sim sandbox idea)
- Evaluate automated rollback heuristics that consider quality signals, not just latency/cost. How often do these heuristics false-positive?
- Should we expand micro-slice matrix to include device-type + SDK-version as default? (early data suggests 6% of contamination traces map to old SDKs)

Appendix: quick references
- Minimal incident timeline template (copy into incident doc).
- Simulation repo: github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-sim (PR#3402 contains oscillation harness).
- Contact: Lina Gupta (triage lead) and Marco Rivera (infra lead)

Notes to self (todo)
- Add a short checklist that the onboarding engineer can click through before enabling exposure >5%.
- Wire automated cohort-overlap detection into the Console experiment summary.

End of note.
